x:
Bats come out at night to hunt for food. Most bats eat insects, like moths, beetles, and mosquitoes. But how do they find tiny bugs in the dark?

Many bats use sound to help them. A bat makes high squeaks that people cannot hear. The sound bounces off a bug and comes back to the bat's ears. Then the bat knows where the bug is, and it flies over to catch it. This is called echolocation. One little bat can eat hundreds of insects in a single night, so bats are good friends to farmers.

Last Saturday, my aunt took me to the aquarium in Boston. I wanted to see the penguins more than anything else. When we got there, the penguins were swimming fast in their tank. They looked like they were flying under the water!

A helper told us that penguins are birds, but they cannot fly in the air. Their wings work like flippers instead. I watched one penguin dive, turn, and zoom back to the top. Before we left, I bought a small book about penguins. I read it in the car on the way home.

Honeybees live together in a big group called a colony. Each colony has one queen bee. She lays all of the eggs. The worker bees do almost everything else. They clean the hive, feed the young bees, and make wax.

Worker bees also fly from flower to flower to collect nectar. Back at the hive, they turn the nectar into honey. Bees need this honey for food in the winter. When a bee finds good flowers, it does a little dance. The dance tells the other bees where to go. Isn't that clever?

The giraffe is the tallest animal on land. A grown giraffe can be taller than a one-story house. Giraffes live in Africa, where they walk across wide, grassy plains.

A giraffe uses its long neck to reach leaves at the tops of trees. Its favorite tree is the acacia, which has sharp thorns. That does not stop the giraffe! Its long, tough tongue can wrap around the leaves and pull them off. Giraffes only need to sleep a few hours each day. They often rest standing up, so they can run if they see danger.

Have you ever put ice cubes in a glass of water? The ice floats at the top. Most things get heavier for their size when they freeze, but water is different.

When water freezes, it spreads out and takes up more space. That makes ice lighter than the same amount of water, so it floats. This is very important for fish. In winter, ice forms on top of ponds and lakes. The ice works like a lid, and the water below it stays liquid. The fish can keep swimming all winter long.

On Monday, our class did a science test with magnets. Our teacher, Mr. Lopez, gave each group a bag of objects. We had a paper clip, a penny, a nail, a pencil, and a spoon.

First, we guessed which things the magnet would pick up. Then we tried each one. The paper clip and the nail jumped right to the magnet. The pencil and the penny did not move at all. I was surprised that the spoon did not stick. Mr. Lopez said magnets only pull on some metals, like iron. Now I want to test everything in my house!

Plants need water to live, but they do not have mouths. So how do they drink? The answer is in their roots.

Roots grow down into the soil. They have tiny hairs that soak up water. The water moves up through the stem, like juice going up a straw. Then it travels out to the leaves. You can see this for yourself. Put a stalk of celery in a cup of water with a few drops of food coloring. Wait a day, and then look at the leaves. They will turn the same color as the water!

Every sound you hear starts with something shaking. When you pluck a guitar string, it moves back and forth very fast. This is called vibrating. The string makes the air around it shake too, and the shaking air travels to your ears.

Try this at home. Put your fingers on your throat and hum a song. Can you feel the buzzing? That is your voice box vibrating. Fast vibrations make high sounds, like a bird's chirp. Slow vibrations make low sounds, like a big drum. Sound can also travel through water, wood, and even walls.

Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun. People call it the Red Planet because its dirt and rocks are a rusty red color. Mars is smaller than Earth, and it is much colder there.

Mars has the biggest volcano in our solar system. It is called Olympus Mons, and it is more than twice as tall as Mount Everest. Scientists have sent robot rovers to drive around on Mars. The rovers take pictures, dig in the dirt, and send their findings back to Earth. Someday, people might visit Mars too.

Last summer, my grandpa set up his telescope in the backyard. He pointed it at a bright dot in the sky. "Take a look," he said. I closed one eye and looked through the tube.

There was Saturn, with its rings all around it! It looked like a tiny toy. Grandpa told me the rings are made of ice and rock. Some pieces are as small as sand, and some are as big as a house. We stayed outside until it was late. I will never forget the night I saw Saturn with my own eyes.

t: Why We Have Day and Night
x:
Earth is always spinning, like a top. It takes about 24 hours to spin around one time. As Earth turns, one side faces the Sun. On that side, it is day. The other side faces away from the Sun, so it is night there.

The Sun looks like it moves across the sky, but it does not really move. We are the ones moving! In the morning, our side of Earth turns toward the Sun, and we see it rise. In the evening, we turn away, and the Sun seems to set. Then the stars come out.

In July 1969, two astronauts landed on the Moon. Their names were Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin. Neil Armstrong was the first person to step onto the Moon's dusty ground.

The Moon has no wind or rain. Because of that, the footprints the astronauts made are still there today. The astronauts collected rocks, took pictures, and put up a flag. They also hopped around, because the Moon's pull is much weaker than Earth's. After their walk, they flew back home. Millions of people watched the landing on TV.

After a rain shower, you might see a rainbow in the sky. A rainbow appears when sunlight shines through tiny drops of water in the air. Sunlight looks white, but it is really made of many colors mixed together.

When light passes through a raindrop, the drop bends the light and splits it into colors. The colors always come in the same order. They are red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet. To see a rainbow, stand with the Sun behind you. You can even make one with a garden hose on a sunny day.

Deep under the ground, it is so hot that some rock melts. This melted rock is called magma. Sometimes the magma pushes up through a crack in Earth's crust. When it comes out, we call it lava, and the place where it comes out is a volcano.

The state of Hawaii is made of volcanoes. In fact, the islands were built by lava that cooled and hardened over a very long time. Some of Hawaii's volcanoes are still active today. Scientists watch them closely, so they can warn people before lava starts to flow.

This spring, our class planted a garden behind the school. We grew beans, carrots, and sunflowers. Every morning, two kids took turns watering the plants.

At first, nothing happened. Then tiny green sprouts poked out of the dirt. My friend Maya and I measured the sunflowers every week. By June, they were taller than our teacher! We learned that plants need sunlight, water, air, and good soil to grow. On the last day of school, we picked the beans and shared them with our families. I can't wait to plant again next year.

When the ocean tide goes out, it leaves small pools of water in the rocks. These are called tide pools. Many little animals live there, like crabs, snails, and sea stars.

Life in a tide pool is not easy. The water gets warm in the sun, and waves crash over the rocks. The animals have smart ways to stay safe. Crabs hide under rocks. Snails close up tight inside their shells. Sea stars hold on with hundreds of tiny tube feet. If you visit a tide pool, look closely, but leave the animals in their home.

Benjamin Franklin lived in Philadelphia over 250 years ago. He was a printer, a writer, and an inventor. He also loved to ask questions about the world.

Franklin wondered if lightning was a kind of electricity. In 1752, he tried a famous test with a kite during a storm. Franklin learned that lightning really is electricity. Then he invented the lightning rod. It is a metal pole on top of a building that carries lightning safely into the ground. Lightning rods still protect many buildings today.

t: A Letter from the Oregon Trail
x:
Dear Grandma,

We have been on the trail for two months now. Our wagon is pulled by four oxen, and I walk next to it most days. Yesterday, we crossed a wide river. Papa was worried, but we all made it across safely.

At night, the families park their wagons in a big circle. We cook beans and bread over the fire, and then we sing songs. I miss you and our old house in Missouri. Mama says we will reach Oregon before the snow comes. I will write again soon.

Love, Sarah

In 1620, a group of people called the Pilgrims sailed from England to America. Their ship was named the Mayflower. They landed in a place that is now Massachusetts.

The first winter was very hard, and they did not have enough food. The Wampanoag people lived nearby. A man named Squanto showed the Pilgrims how to plant corn and catch fish. In the fall of 1621, the Pilgrims had a good harvest. They held a big feast, and the Wampanoag joined them. Today, many Americans remember this feast on Thanksgiving.

Harriet Tubman was born into slavery in Maryland around 1822. When she was a young woman, she escaped to the North, where she could be free. But she did not stop there.

Tubman went back south many times to help others escape. She led them along a secret path called the Underground Railroad. It was not a real train. It was a group of safe houses and helpers. Tubman traveled at night and used the North Star to find her way. She helped about 70 people reach freedom, and she never lost a single one.

Japan is a country in Asia made up of many islands. Its capital city is Tokyo, which is one of the biggest cities in the world. Japan also has a famous mountain called Mount Fuji.

In Japan, many people eat with chopsticks. Rice, fish, and noodles are popular foods. When people meet, they often bow instead of shaking hands. Every spring, cherry trees bloom with pink flowers all over the country. Families and friends have picnics under the trees to enjoy the blossoms. Would you like to visit Japan someday?

A map is a drawing of a place seen from above. Maps help us find our way. Most maps have a few special parts that make them easier to read.

The compass rose shows the directions north, south, east, and west. The key, or legend, tells what the symbols mean. A small tree might stand for a park, and a blue line might be a river. Some maps also have a scale. It shows how far apart places really are. Last week, I drew a map of my neighborhood. I put my house, my school, and the library on it.

Over winter break, my family visited Mexico City. It is the capital of Mexico, and it is a huge, busy city. My mom grew up there, so she was our tour guide.

On the first day, we went to a giant park called Chapultepec. It has a lake, a zoo, and a castle on a hill! The next day, we ate tacos, tamales, and sweet bread from a bakery. I practiced my Spanish with the waiter, and he smiled at me. My favorite part was riding a colorful boat on the canals of Xochimilco. I hope we go back soon.

The Nile is one of the longest rivers in the world. It flows north through Africa for more than 4,000 miles. It ends at the Mediterranean Sea in the country of Egypt.

Most of Egypt is a hot, dry desert. Long ago, the people of Egypt lived close to the Nile, because it gave them water. Every year, the river flooded and left rich mud on the land. Farmers used this mud to grow wheat and other crops. The ancient Egyptians also used the river like a road. They sailed boats up and down it to trade.

Every Saturday, my dad and I make pancakes. First, we get out the flour, milk, eggs, and a big bowl. I crack the eggs, and Dad measures the flour. Then I stir everything together until it is smooth.

Dad heats the pan, and I pour in a little circle of batter. When bubbles pop on top, it is time to flip it. Last week, I flipped one too high, and it landed on the floor! We both laughed. My little sister likes her pancakes with strawberries. I like mine with butter and syrup.

Two weeks ago, we brought home a new puppy. His name is Biscuit, and he is brown and white. He has big floppy ears and a tail that never stops wagging.

Taking care of a puppy is a lot of work. Every morning, I fill his bowl with food and fresh water. After school, I take him for a walk around the block. Biscuit likes to chew on everything, so we bought him some chew toys. He still chewed one of my socks, though! At night, he sleeps in a basket next to my bed. I love him so much.

On Sundays, everyone in our family helps clean the house. Mom calls it Chore Day. We each pick a job from a jar. This week, I got the job of folding the laundry.

My brother Jake had to sweep the kitchen, and my sister Lily dusted the shelves. Dad washed the windows, and Mom cleaned the bathroom. It took us about an hour. When we were done, the whole house looked bright and shiny. Then we all sat down to watch a movie together. Chore Day is more fun than it sounds, because we do it as a team.

Yesterday, I could not find my lunchbox anywhere. I looked in my backpack, under my desk, and in the coat closet. It was not there. My stomach was growling, and I started to worry.

Then my friend Omar had an idea. "Did you check the bus?" he asked. I ran to the office, and the secretary called the bus driver. My lunchbox was sitting on a seat! The driver brought it to school after his route. I ate my sandwich, my apple, and my cookies a little late, but I was very happy.

On Saturday, my soccer team, the Tigers, played against the Hawks. It was a sunny day, and lots of families came to watch. I play defense, so my job is to stop the other team from scoring.

In the first half, the Hawks scored a goal. We were sad, but our coach told us to keep trying. In the second half, my friend Ana kicked the ball into the net! Then I stopped a fast player, and Leo scored again. We won the game two to one. After the game, we shared orange slices and cheered for both teams.

Hopscotch is a fun game you can play outside. All you need is chalk, a small stone, and a flat sidewalk. First, draw eight boxes on the ground and number them from 1 to 8.

To start, toss your stone into box 1. Then hop over that box and through the rest of the boxes. Use one foot for single boxes and two feet for side-by-side boxes. At the end, turn around and hop back. Pick up your stone on the way. If you step on a line or fall, your turn is over. Then it is your friend's turn.

Basketball was invented in 1891 by a teacher named James Naismith. He taught at a school in Springfield, Massachusetts. In the winter, it was too cold for his students to play outside, so he needed an indoor game.

Naismith nailed two peach baskets to the walls of the gym. The players tried to toss a soccer ball into the baskets. Every time someone scored, a person had to climb a ladder to get the ball out! Later, people cut holes in the bottom of the baskets. Today, basketball is played all over the world.

This summer, I took swimming lessons at the city pool. On the first day, I was scared to put my face in the water. My teacher, Ms. Kim, was very patient with me.

First, we practiced blowing bubbles. Then we learned to float on our backs. Ms. Kim held my back until I felt safe. By the third week, I could kick my legs and move my arms at the same time. On the last day, I swam all the way across the pool by myself! My parents clapped and cheered. Now I want to swim every day.

Our class put on a play about the three little pigs. I was the wolf, and I had to huff and puff very loudly. My friend Grace was the first pig, and she built a house of straw.

We practiced every day for three weeks. Our teacher painted the houses, and we made the costumes ourselves. On the night of the play, I was so nervous that my hands were shaking. But when the lights came on, I remembered all my lines. The audience laughed when I fell down the chimney. At the end, everyone stood up and clapped.

Did you know you can make lots of colors with just three? Red, yellow, and blue are called the primary colors. You can mix them to make new colors.

If you mix red and yellow, you get orange. Yellow and blue make green, and blue and red make purple. These are called secondary colors. You can also add white to make a color lighter, or add black to make it darker. Yesterday, I tried mixing paints at the kitchen table. I made a sky blue, a bright orange, and a muddy brown. Then I painted a picture of a sunset.

My favorite book is about a girl who finds a secret door in her grandma's attic. Behind the door, there is a magical garden. The flowers can talk, and the trees tell jokes.

I like this book because it is funny and exciting. The girl is brave, and she helps a lost rabbit find its family. I have read it four times! Every time I read it, I notice something new in the pictures. My brother says he likes comic books better than chapter books. I think he should give this book a try.

You can make your own music at home with glass jars and water. First, line up five jars on a table. Pour a little water into the first jar. Pour a bit more into the next one, and keep going until the last jar is almost full.

Now tap each jar gently with a metal spoon. Listen to the sounds. The jar with the most water makes the lowest note, and the jar with the least water makes the highest note. Try tapping them in different orders to play a song. My sister and I played a tune for our parents, and they loved it.

Long ago, people used candles and oil lamps to see at night. These lights were dim, and they could start fires. Many inventors wanted to make a better light.

In 1879, Thomas Edison and his team made a light bulb that could glow for many hours. Inside the glass bulb was a thin thread called a filament. When electricity flowed through it, the filament got hot and gave off light. Edison tested thousands of materials before he found one that worked well. Soon, homes and streets all over the country had electric lights.

A bicycle is a simple machine that helps you move faster than walking. When you push the pedals, they turn a wheel with teeth called a gear. A chain goes around this gear and another gear on the back wheel.

As the chain moves, it turns the back wheel, and the bike rolls forward. The handlebars let you steer left or right. When you squeeze the brakes, rubber pads press on the wheels and slow them down. Bikes don't need gas, so they are good for the air. My friends and I ride our bikes to the park every weekend.

Before the telephone, people sent letters or used telegraphs to share news. Letters could take weeks to arrive. Then, in 1876, Alexander Graham Bell got a patent for the telephone.

The first telephones turned a person's voice into an electric signal. The signal traveled through a wire to another phone, and that phone turned it back into sound. At first, only a few homes had phones. Over time, wires stretched across the whole country. Today, most phones don't need wires at all, and we can call people almost anywhere in the world.

For the science fair, I built a little robot with my older cousin Theo. We used a kit with wheels, a small motor, and a battery. Theo showed me how to connect the wires.

Then we wrote a few simple directions on his laptop. We told the robot to go forward, turn left, and stop when it got close to a wall. The first time we tried it, the robot spun in circles! We fixed a mistake in our directions, and then it worked. At the fair, the judges liked our robot, and we won a blue ribbon.
